title: Logistics Ruling: Lateness End Date by Branch Arrival — Factory Production Orders
content:
**Ruling.** For Factory Production Orders, the lateness end date of the on-time guarantee — the date the full weeks late are measured to from the end of the grace period — is set by how the units reached the branch:

1. when the order was delivered to the branch **later than** its ship date plus the class transit time in business days, it is the **branch delivery date**;
2. when it was delivered **on or before** that expected arrival, it is the **expected arrival date**, the ship date plus the class transit time in business days;
3. when it has not been delivered, it is the **ship date**.

The ship date is the date the last unit of the order shipped (the class lateness ship basis, last unit shipped), and the expected arrival is counted from it in business days, Monday through Friday excluding U.S. federal holidays, starting the day after the ship date. The full weeks late are the calendar days from the end of the grace period to the lateness end date, divided by seven and rounded down.

## Class transit time (business days)

| Build class | Transit |
|---|---|
| Custom Size Build | 2 |
| Custom Color Build | 2 |
| Specialty Glass Build | 2 |
| Specialty Shape Build | 3 |
| Impact-Rated Build | 3 |
| Architectural Wood Build | 3 |

## Both sides of the expected arrival (hypothetical Custom Color Build order shipped on a Monday, no federal holiday that week)

| Branch delivery | Expected arrival | Lateness end date |
|---|---|---|
| Thursday | Wednesday | Thursday (delivered later than expected) |
| Wednesday | Wednesday | Wednesday (on the expected arrival) |
| Tuesday | Wednesday | Wednesday (earlier than expected) |
| not yet delivered | — | the Monday ship date |

## Records read

The ship date and the branch delivery date on the factory order record.
